title: Core configuration
description: Asked for every project. Everything here has a configuration consequence; a question that changes nothing is deleted, not kept for colour.

questions.rationale: Decides how much you are asked. The --mode flag overrides this.

questions.ask: Which framework profile fits this project?
questions.rationale: S is one agent and two registries; L is the full roster. Starting at L on a small project makes the framework the bottleneck it exists to remove.

questions.ask: What kind of system is this?
questions.rationale: Selects the documentation profile and the question packs that follow.

questions.ask: Which decisions may agents take without asking you?
questions.rationale: This is the escalation boundary every builder is held to. It is the one setting worth your attention even in a hurry.
Changes the builder protocol and what the task gate demands.

questions.ask: Rank the non-functional priorities that should decide close calls.
questions.rationale: These are the comparison criteria for architecture options and the focus order for review lenses. Without them the agent invents its own.

questions.ask: How strict should automated review be?
questions.rationale: Picks the lens matrix. Strict roughly doubles review cost per task.

questions.ask: How are this project's packages tested, linted and built?
questions.rationale: The gate runs exactly these commands. A monorepo declares one entry per package so a task only pays for what it touched.

questions.ask: Which paths must agents never modify?
questions.rationale: Copied into the constitution and enforced by the write-lease check. Empty is a valid answer for a greenfield project.

questions.ask: Who owns exemptions, and which checks may an agent waive in their name?
questions.rationale: A waiver is owned by a person who can be asked. Naming that person once, with the checks they delegate (for example docs and env), lets an agent record a routine waiver without a call; a finding waiver is never delegated. The default is empty, which changes nothing: every waiver is then recorded by hand. A person opts in with `aegis answer q.core.delegate` and the shape {"owner": "<name>", "may_waive": ["docs"]}.
